What is Star Anise ?

Star Anise supplies high end desserts, cakes, pastries, breads, snacks & much more to cafes, restaurants, banquet halls, pastry shops, weddings and corporate cafes.. Highly trained staff, world class products, well presented desserts & on time logistics support make us your preferred go to pastry shop.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Walking into this bakery always feels comforting—familiar aromas, shelves full of freshly baked goodness, and the assurance that you’ll walk out with something you’ll genuinely enjoy. Theobroma Bakery has built that kind of trust over time, especially for those who value quality over gimmicks.

Their fresh sourdough and artisanal breads are absolute standouts and personal favourites—beautifully crusted, well-fermented, and full of character. The quiches and tarts are consistently satisfying, with buttery bases and well-balanced fillings that make them reliable picks every time. The tea cakes are another strong point: soft, moist, and understated, making them perfect companions to coffee or tea.

The pastry and cake counter is equally impressive, offering a wide range of flavours—from indulgent chocolate classics to lighter, nuanced options. Each dessert feels thoughtfully made, never overly sweet, and always well-executed. What’s equally commendable is the good balance of savoury items, which adds depth to the menu and keeps things interesting beyond desserts.

It’s the kind of place you return to not just for cravings, but for consistency, comfort, and the quiet joy of well-made food.

Its our first time in the city and the shop. We asked for recommendations and the guy billing wasn't even interested in telling us anything and was ignoring us. The girl placed the two items that were ordered by us in a tray when she called the items, ( not the order no. or something which they don't have) we walked up to her and she was rude to us. He told her two times before she told the other lady who was polite to pick our items up from the shelf and went with the tray in her hand to the guy and was taking pictures of the tray with her phone and talking to the guy. And we didn't see the group of people with camera with the similar tray of desserts that we ordered. Maybe we missed them eating that or something and maybe they did
order just before us and their order was severely delayed or something cause it was taking time for us to complete the whole billing process. But order delivery should be kind of fast for all the desserts as they just take them out from the shelf in front. We felt insulted and if we hadn't already paid the bill we would have walked out. This made the atmosphere tense for us and made the entire experience bad.

featured_reviews.name: i12
featured_reviews.review_text:
A tidy and well kept café in the heart of the Fort area. It is relatively quiet for the location, which makes it a comfortable place to sit rather than just grab and go.

Coffee was acceptable rather than memorable. The cappuccino and Americano did the job without standing out. The pastry selection was uneven. The dark chocolate mousse pastry was well done and rich, the Dutch truffles pastry was ordinary, while the fresh cream pineapple pastry was genuinely good.

One moment felt slightly awkward. At the counter, the cashier suggested he could lower the bill by around Rs 12 by entering a different coffee option into the system, and asked whether I would prefer that. I am sure the intention was to be helpful, but it came across as unnecessary and a little uncomfortable.

Overall, a decent stop for pastries & coffee in Fort.

I am writing to share some feedback regarding my recent experience.

While the overall atmosphere seems to be positive, I found the taste of the items to be average, and I felt the experience was more hype-driven. The sweet bakery items were noticeably better than the non-vegetarian offerings, which were disappointing.

In terms of value, the pricing seems very expensive compared to other bakeries, especially considering the lack of specialized options like low-fat or flour-less products.

Additionally, I would like to bring up an issue with the home delivery service. Even on a purchase of ₹10,000, a delivery fee is applied. Furthermore, the items are delivered via Ola/Uber taxi instead of a standard delivery service like Porter or Swiggy, which results in an excessive delivery charge.

Ambience & Service:

Overall Experience:
Edward Bakery is more than just a place to grab a bite—it's a slice of Mumbai's culinary history. Whether you're in the mood for their famous puffs, freshly baked bread, or a variety of other bakery items, you won't be disappointed. The consistent quality and freshness of their offerings make it a beloved spot for both locals and visitors alike.

If you're in Fort, make sure to stop by Edward Bakery for a taste of tradition and some truly delicious treats!

featured_reviews.name: Sourajyoti
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery is one of those places in Mumbai that feels frozen in time. Started in 1953, it has been run by the same family for generations and still carries the old Irani café charm. The bakery is located in an old heritage building near Fort and Colaba, and the moment you step inside, you feel like you’ve walked into a different era — with its wooden furniture, old photographs, and simple, no-nonsense setup.
Yazdani is best known for its brun maska (soft bun with butter) and Irani chai, which is probably the most popular order here. Their mawa cake is legendary — rich, soft and full of flavour — and often sells out quickly. Other favourites include khari biscuits, apple pie, plum cake, and freshly baked breads and cookies. Everything tastes homemade and fresh, which is what keeps people coming back.
The place is not fancy, and service is simple, but that’s part of its charm. You come here not for luxury, but for nostalgia, honest food, and a slice of old Bombay. If you want to experience Mumbai’s Irani café culture and enjoy some classic bakery items, Yazdani is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery Takeaway: A Taste of Nostalgia
Yazdani Bakery is more than just a place to grab a bite; it's a living monument to Mumbai’s Irani cafe heritage. Opting for a takeaway from this institution is a smart choice for those eager to savor its legendary bakes without the old-school dine-in experience (currently limited anyway).
The magic lies in the Brun Maska—a crusty, yet tender, bread generously slathered with creamy butter—and the dense, aromatic Mawa Cake. These staples are impeccably fresh, a testament to the bakery's commitment to quality ingredients and traditional wood-fire ovens. Don't overlook the Shrewsbury Biscuits or the flaky, savory Khari. Packaging is basic and efficient—perfectly functional for transport.
While the interior retains a charmingly worn, antique aesthetic, the focus here is the edible legacy. The staff can occasionally be brisk, but the efficiency ensures a quick transaction. A Yazdani takeaway isn't just buying baked goods; it's securing a comforting, consistent piece of culinary history to enjoy in your own space. It's an indispensable, buttery, sweet slice of Mumbai.

This small outlet is located within a dense commercial/residential area. You'd need a cab to get here because parking was a little difficult.

There isn't a lot of seating. Only one table is there in the AC area and another in the outside seating area. There isn't any music available and the lighting was really off. The lights kept flickering. We had to request that they be switched off.

We first went in for the 24-layer Pastry. This is a very good dessert. Even though there are so many layers of cream and cake, the dessert wasn't very heavy. It's great for sharing.

The next came the Red Velvet Pastry. There's no other way to describe it than just plain terrible. This is the worst version of this cake I have had so far. The cake looked a little slumped when it was served to us but we didn't think much about it. With one small slice, the entire pastry collapsed. The cake itself wasn't so good and the icing was very off. There were instances where we thought this might be a cheesecake but it wasn't. The cake had a room temperature which might indicate that the refrigeration of the desserts aren't up to the mark.

I'm not pleased with the variation in the quality of desserts. One was good while the other was terrible making it difficult for me to recommend this place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
"Merwans Cake Shop is my go-to place for birthday cakes, as they always deliver on freshness and taste. However, what truly stole my heart are their Irish Coffee Cake and Blueberry Cheesecake. These two desserts are absolute delights, bursting with flavor and leaving me craving for more with every bite.

But it doesn't stop there—their confectionary items, such as the mini pizza rolls, are equally exceptional. Each bite is a delightful explosion of flavors, and I'm always amazed by how fresh and tasty they are. The best part is that all of these delectable items come at very affordable prices, making it even more enticing to indulge in their offerings.

In addition to their cakes and confectionary treats, Merwans Cake Shop also serves a range of refreshing beverages. Their thick shakes, juices, and soft-serve ice creams are the perfect accompaniment to their delectable desserts.

The menu at Merwans Cake Shop is extensive, and I've tried nearly every item on it. Without fail, each treat has left me impressed with its quality and taste. The bakery takes pride in delivering fresh, flavorful creations, and they consistently succeed in doing so.

If you're a cake lover or simply have a sweet tooth, I highly recommend visiting Merwans Cake Shop. You'll be treated to an array of scrumptious cakes, mouthwatering confectionary items, and refreshing beverages—all at prices that won't break the bank. Give it a try and prepare to be delighted!"
